It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals fitted as routine maintenance, and other consumables are excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. It applies to every claim submitted through the service claim system.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Interpretation\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1.4  Precedence between instruments\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere two or more instruments address the same asset, the order of precedence is: (a) a Technical Service Bulletin that names the serial range of the asset; (b) the Regional Addendum for the region in which the asset is installed; (c) this policy. A Bulletin that has been superseded has no effect, whether or not it remains published. Where the Bulletin document and the service system applicability index disagree, the Bulletin document governs; the index is maintained for reporting and is informational only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Coverage\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.1  Standard coverage period\\r\\n  \\r\\nUnless extended or varied by an instrument of higher precedence, an asset is covered for twenty-four (24) months from the date of commissioning, or six thousand (6,000) running hours, whichever occurs first.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2.3  Assets with no commissioning record\\r\\n  \\r\\nWhere the commissioning record for an asset is absent from the asset registry, coverage cannot be determined. The claim is to be held and the commissioning certificate requested from the installing partner. The date of despatch or the date of installation must not be substituted for the date of commissioning.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Amounts payable\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.1  Labour\\r\\n  \\r\\nLabour is payable at the flat-rate allowance published for the operation code in the current Flat Rate Labour schedule, or at the hours actually claimed, whichever is the lesser. The rate applied is the regional labour rate in force on the date of repair.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.2  Parts\\r\\n  \\r\\nParts are payable at the published list price for the region, for the part actually fitted. Where a part has been superseded, the price of the superseding part applies.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 4.3  Handling\\r\\n  \\r\\nA handling uplift on parts is payable only where the partner\\u0027s Service Partner Agreement expressly grants one, at the percentage stated in that agreement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Exclusions\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.1  Exclusion - misuse and overload\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from operation outside the published duty envelope, including sustained overload, is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.2  Exclusion - fluid contamination\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from hydraulic fluid contamination above ISO 4406 class 18/16/13 is excluded, save where a Technical Service Bulletin provides otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.3  Exclusion - unauthorised modification\\r\\n  \\r\\nDamage arising from modification not authorised in writing by Contoso Industrial is excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 5.4  Exclusion - consumables\\r\\n  \\r\\nFilters, fluids, belts, seals fitted as routine maintenance, and other consumables are excluded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Repair warranty\\r\\n\\r\\n### 6.1  Repair warranty\\r\\n  \\r\\nA component replaced under warranty carries a further ninety (90) days of coverage from the date the repair was completed. A claim arising within that period is adjudicated under this clause and carries funding code RW, whether or not the underlying asset remains within its coverage period.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. Goodwill and authority\\r\\n\\r\\n### 7.1  Goodwill authority\\r\\n  \\r\\nAn amount payable outside coverage may be authorised as goodwill only by a person holding the tier of authority set out in the Goodwill and Authority Matrix for that amount, and only where the authority is recorded in the claim system. # Decision — approve

**Claim C-2026-04101 should be approved for INR 69,575.** The repair is covered under the **India Regional Addendum ADD-IN-2.1**, read with the Global Warranty Policy **POL-WAR-4.2**. I recorded draft adjudication **ADJ-4AC1CB7AD9** as an approval for **INR 69,575**; it is awaiting human review and no payment has been made.

## Why the repair is covered

- The claim is for asset **CIE-4000-CH-01050**, a 4000-CH industrial chiller installed in **Pune, India**, commissioned on **15 March 2025**.
- Under **POL-WAR-4.2 clause 1.4**, an applicable serial-specific bulletin takes precedence, followed by the regional addendum and then the global policy.
- **TSB-C-0051 does not apply.** Its published document covers only serials **CIE-4000-CH-01200 through CIE-4000-CH-01850**, and only hydraulic-circuit and compressor coverage. This asset is serial **…01050**, and the repair was to the **control board**.
- Therefore, **ADD-IN-2.1 A1** governs the coverage period because the asset is installed in India. It provides **18 months from commissioning or 5,000 running hours, whichever occurs first**.
- The time limb runs from **15 March 2025 to 15 September 2026**. The repair on **10 May 2026** occurred about 14 months after commissioning and before that time limit.
- The field inspection report records **2,400 running hours at repair**, below the 5,000-hour limit. It states that the control board was unresponsive, was replaced, and showed **no evidence of moisture ingress or surge damage**.
- The claim system’s latest meter reading was **2,229 hours on 15 April 2026**, rather than a reading on the repair date. This differs from the inspection report’s 2,400-hour reading because the readings are dated 25 days apart; both remain well below 5,000 hours, so the difference does not affect coverage.
- The claim was submitted on **16 May 2026**, six days after the repair and within Fabrikam’s 30-day submission SLA.

## Payable calculation

| Element | Working | Payable |
|---|---:|---:|
| Labour | Lesser of **1.5 hours claimed** and **1.5 flat-rate hours** for CTRL-BD-RR = 1.5 hours; **1.5 × INR 1,450/hour** | **INR 2,175** |
| Part | One control board **P-44900**, the part actually fitted; no supersession; India list price | **INR 67,400** |
| Partner handling uplift | Fabrikam agreement SPA-2023-FAB-IN expressly provides **no handling uplift**; 0% × INR 67,400 | **INR 0** |
| **Total** | INR 2,175 + INR 67,400 + INR 0 | **INR 69,575** |

The FY26 flat-rate schedule allows 1.5 hours for CTRL-BD-RR, and the regional rate card sets the India rate at INR 1,450 per hour for repairs from 1 April 2026 through 31 March 2027. The service history confirms that P-44900 was actually fitted and that 1.5 hours were worked; the parts record prices that current, non-superseded part at INR 67,400. Fabrikam’s agreement uses INR and grants no parts uplift.

## Instrument and source reconciliation

- **Governing coverage instrument:** ADD-IN-2.1 A1.
- **Supporting pricing provisions:** POL-WAR-4.2 clauses 4.1–4.3, Flat-Rate-Labour-FY26, Labour-Rates-By-Region-FY26, the parts record, and SPA-2023-FAB-IN.
- **Bulletin applicability:** The claim-system bulletin index is informational only. It says TSB-C-0051 is not in range, which agrees with the authoritative bulletin document for this asset. The bulletin document controls in any event under policy clause 1.4.
- **Meter-reading difference:** 2,229 hours in the registry as of 15 April versus 2,400 hours in the inspection report on 10 May. This is noted in the draft but is not outcome-determinative because both readings are below the 5,000-hour ceiling.
- **No goodwill issue:** No goodwill was requested, and none is required because the repair is within normal India warranty coverage.

## What happens next

The **Warranty Operations adjudicator** should review and finalize draft **ADJ-4AC1CB7AD9**. On final approval, the claim should proceed through the normal settlement workflow for **INR 69,575**. No evidence request or goodwill escalation is required.
